subject.title: fix(agents): bound stalled SSH directory uploads with an idle watchdog

question: Is a default 30-second zero-progress cutoff acceptable for existing SSH sandbox uploads, including remote hosts whose transfers can legitimately pause without emitting tar output?
rationale: The patch is deliberately compatibility-changing: it converts an indefinite zero-progress wait into a process kill and rejection, while current callers do not select the timeout themselves.

options.title: Accept the progress watchdog
options.body: Approve the 30-second zero-progress default as the supported failure boundary for sandbox uploads and merge after ordinary CI review.

options.title: Make the bound caller-owned
options.body: Retain the watchdog mechanism but require the sandbox owner to supply the timeout if maintainers do not want a new global default.

options.title: Pause for broader transfer semantics
options.body: Defer the PR if a long silent pause is considered a supported upload state that needs a different product contract.

recommendation.title: Accept the progress watchdog
recommendation.body: Approve the 30-second zero-progress default as the supported failure boundary for sandbox uploads and merge after ordinary CI review.

likelyOwner.reason: Best available low-confidence routing candidate for the agent-sandbox compatibility decision identified in the previous review.
